newsitem.title: UK: British houseware retail market set to boom - study.
newsitem.headline: British houseware retail market set to boom - study.

text.p: The British housewares and home furnishings market is set to be a "booming market" over the next few years, underpinned by steady improvement in the housing market, according to research group Verdict.

In a report on housewares retailers, Verdict said the market was "one of the least developed in UK retailing...(and) among the most attractive opportunities which remains to be exploited in an otherwise mature retail market."
Verdict said the market was currently worth 6.8 billion stg with sales in the second half of 1996 growing by some eight percent.
It said Argos was "well placed in the long term to become the market leader."
Argos, which sells through catalogues at its stores, has a "relatively wide offer, competitive pricing and...reliance on branding," Verdict said.
But it warned the chain would need to extend ranges to realise its potential.

Verdict said the John Lewis Partnership chain had "undoubted strengths (which) should underpin its leading role in this sector," and has made a 0.4 point gain in market share, equalled only by Argos, to take just over five percent of the market.
Verdict said the sector had "a high degree of fragmentation," however, with brands dominating but the research group said there were opportunities to create "distinctive own label ranges."
It said out-of-town retailing had made little impact on the sector, adding that none of these players matched high street outlets in depth of range.
Verdict said continental group IKEA was able to benefit from increasing internationalisation of design and could sell anywhere in Europe, enabling it to capitalise on buying strength.
"The company plans an active opening programme and is well set to become a major force in UK housewares retailing," Verdict said.
It added that retailers such as Marks & Spencer, Next, Habitat and Laura Ashley "are creating houseware ranges that are an integral part of the lifestyle branding of their businesses."

Verdict said specialists such as Next, Habitat and Laura Ashley brought "a distinctive handwriting to their product offer," and other housewares retailers should look to their success when planning future ranges.
